claims.head: There’s no curse: Vejmelka against the Oilers
claims.body: Since 2023-24, Vejmelka has been shaky against the Oilers, well below his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if he’s back to his usual self.
claims.nums: 7 starts against Edmonton: .858 save percentage · .899 against everyone else
claims.gist: Don’t read much into Vejmelka’s record against the Oilers.
claims.call: If Vejmelka starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .899 than to his .858 against the Oilers.
claims.cite: Goalie starts since 2023-24 · 7 against Edmonton, 4,061 shots against everyone else

chips.tip: Vejmelka: .858 save percentage in 7 starts against Edmonton since 2023-24.
Vejmelka: .899 save percentage against everyone else since 2023-24, on 4,061 shots.

claims.head: The Mammoth roll four lines, the Oilers lean on their top six
claims.body: On depth, Utah is the league’s best, but Edmonton is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Mammoth.

notes.text: Zach Hyman has not dressed for the last 6 games. He is a top-six forward.
Ryan Nugent-Hopkins is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has not played this season. He is a top-six forward.
Matt Savoie is on long-term injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has not played this season. Leon Draisaitl has taken his spot beside Connor McDavid and Vasily Podkolzin.
Filip Hållander joined from PIT on Oct 7 and has played beside Jason Dickinson and Kasperi Kapanen.
Kasperi Kapanen has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 59% of the team’s power-play time in 7 games, up from 6% last season.
Ty Emberson is no longer killing penalties: 3% of the team’s shorthanded time in 5 games, down from 30% last season.

UTA.head: The Mammoth have a slight edge
UTA.body: Utah has been out-chancing opponents lately and has home-ice advantage, but they will be without Carcone, and Edmonton gets Hyman back. The Oilers can still swing it if their power play gets going.

EDM.head: A slightly uphill night for the Oilers
EDM.body: Utah has been out-chancing opponents lately and has home-ice advantage, but Edmonton gets Hyman back, and the Mammoth will be without Carcone. The Oilers’ best way to tip it is a power play that gets going.

story.head: McDavid’s favorite opponent
paras: The Mammoth won the first meeting this season, 4-2 in Edmonton. The Mammoth have won three straight. The Oilers are 5-1-1.
Don’t read much into Vejmelka’s record against the Oilers. Expect plenty of hitting.

items.text: The Oilers are newly without Frederik Andersen, have been without Zach Hyman since Sep 29, and have had to make do without Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Matt Savoie all season. Tristan Jarry is expected to start.
Connor McDavid has a point in seven straight games against Utah, and 14 points in his last seven against them.
Barrett Hayton has a point in five straight games.
Evan Bouchard has a point in four straight games.
